title: Brazil elections: Merz, world leaders congratulate Lula on his win
summary: Brazilian President Lula secured a surprise win over far-right challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, who has refused to concede. DW has the latest.
byline: Matt Ford, Akanksha Saxena, Richard Connor, Alex Berry

image.caption: Lula won a fourth term in the runoff despite having trailed Flavio Bolsonaro in the first round of votingImage: Raquel Cunha/REUTERS

blocks.text: Flavio Bolsonaro says he is banned from leaving Brazil after election defeat

blocks.caption: Flavio Bolsonaro denies he has any plans to leave Brazil after his election defeat to Lula Image: Eraldo Peres/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro says he has been ordered to surrender his passports and is banned from leaving the country.
The right-wing senator said federal police approached him after he visited his imprisoned father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.
"I was ordered right on the street to hand over my passports, and I'm also prohibited from leaving the country," Bolsonaro said in a video posted on social media.

He called the move "a clear attempt to intimidate me" and claimed the order came from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes. Neither the court nor federal police immediately confirmed the reported ruling.

Bolsonaro said the decision was based on comments by his brother Eduardo, who had suggested he should leave Brazil if he lost the election. He denied having any plans to flee the country and said he would comply with the order.
